rawCandidates.title: Daily-consolidation dry-run still hard-deletes expired memories
rawCandidates.source: An operator or caller invokes exported runConsolidation with opts.dryRun=true.
rawCandidates.control: The dry-run flag is propagated to dynamics, Neo pruning, compaction, conflict resolution, reporting, and rate-state writes, but not to TTL purge.
rawCandidates.sink: db.purgeExpired calls MemoryDB.purgeExpired, which executes LanceDB table.delete for expired non-core rows.
rawCandidates.impact: A purported non-mutating audit run irreversibly deletes expired memory rows without archive or destructive-operation audit evidence.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: The dry-run branch inconsistency and hard-delete sink are code-complete. Validation must identify every production/API caller that can set dryRun and test a table double proving purgeExpired is invoked during dry-run.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires an authorized operator/caller and at least one expired non-core row. No untrusted remote trigger is currently established; impact is operator-confusion/data loss.

rawCandidates.title: Daily-consolidation lock path interpolates an unvalidated agent identifier
rawCandidates.source: commandCtx.agentId is passed as agent to runConsolidation.
rawCandidates.control: There is no safeAgentId or resolveInside validation before the lock filename is constructed.
rawCandidates.sink: acquireJobLock creates consolidation-${agent}.lock beneath a joined workspace locks path and releaseJobLock later removes it.
rawCandidates.impact: A separator-bearing agent identifier could create/remove a lock file outside the intended locks directory, subject to the fixed prefix/suffix and filesystem permissions.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Unsafe construction is confirmed; validate host guarantees for commandCtx.agentId and exact acquire/release path semantics.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires influence over host agentId, not merely command arguments. The fixed consolidation- prefix limits traversal unless the supplied value contains separators; the .lock suffix remains.
